title: The lifecycle hooks, and which of them you actually need

videos.script:
A component has a life. It is created, it is given its inputs, it is drawn, checked again and again, and one day removed. {{hooks}} Angular can call a method of yours at each of those moments, and those methods are the lifecycle hooks. There are eight. You watch every one of them fire, in order, from a component that logs its own life.

{{init}} Then the reason most of them exist. Inputs are not set in the constructor, so older code waited for ng-on-init. Read a required input in a constructor today, and the compiler stops you.

{{changes}} Reacting to an input used to mean ng-on-changes and a copied field. Now it is a computed. {{destroy}} Cleaning up still matters. You start a clock in a component, remove the component, and the clock keeps ticking. Destroy-ref stops it. {{render}} And after-next-render is the place for code that needs the page drawn.

{{which}} By the end, you know which hooks you will write, which is very few, and which you will only read.
